name: ffmpeg
notes: First FFmpeg port for libcrtmedia's demux/software-decode work (TODO.md, HISTORY.md 2026-08-31's frame-contract entry -- this recipe is the very next step). Deliberately narrow scope for a first landing, matching this project's own established narrow-now-expand-later pattern (curl.json's own HTTP/HTTPS-only first pass is the closest precedent): local file demux only (--enable-protocol=file, --disable-network -- no http/rtsp/etc. yet), one container (mov -- covers MP4/MOV/M4A), one video codec (h264) and three audio codecs (aac/mp3/pcm_s16le) via --disable-everything + explicit --enable-decoder/--enable-demuxer/--enable-parser. No avdevice (capture/playback devices, irrelevant to file decode), no avfilter (this pass calls libswscale/libswresample directly, no filter graph needed), no encode.

License: this recipe deliberately never passes --enable-gpl or --enable-nonfree (both already default-off; there is no --disable- counterpart for either flag in ffmpeg's own configure -- confirmed directly by grepping configure's option parser, so passing --disable-gpl/--disable-nonfree explicitly would itself be a configure error, 'Unknown option'). H.264/AAC/MP3/PCM decode are all native LGPL components, so an LGPL-only build covers this pass's entire codec set with no GPL-licensed code involved. Per LICENSE.md's own stated policy for porting/recipes/*, FFmpeg's source is never committed to this repository -- its own license applies to whatever tools/crt-port-build.py downloads/builds; this note is the documentation of that choice, matching every other recipe's own convention (no recipe.json schema field for license exists anywhere in this porting system, confirmed).

--disable-x86asm/--disable-inline-asm: a deliberate, accepted first-pass tradeoff, not an oversight. FFmpeg's assembly-optimized decode paths need NASM/yasm as a build-time tool, which this project's toolchain does not provide (every other porting recipe here builds with plain C only). Portable C decode is slower than hand-written SIMD asm, but correctness and a working build come first; revisit once a real performance need is demonstrated, matching this project's own established 'no speculative work ahead of a demonstrated need' convention.

libpostproc does not exist in this FFmpeg version at all (confirmed directly: grepping configure's own LIBRARY_LIST finds avdevice/avfilter/swscale/avformat/avcodec/swresample/avutil only, no postproc) -- an earlier draft of this recipe's own configure_args included a stray --disable-postproc that would have failed configure outright ('Unknown option') had it not been caught before the first real build attempt.

8.1.2 (2026-06-17, the '8.1 Hoare' branch's latest point release) is FFmpeg's current stable release as of this port. No published SHA256 exists on ffmpeg.org's own download page (only PGP signatures) -- the checksums recorded above were computed directly against the downloaded tarball, matching every other recipe's own real-hash-computed convention here, not copied from a third party.

Confirmed for real (2026-08-31, first WSL/Linux build attempt): ./configure's own summary matched every intended decoder/demuxer/parser/protocol exactly (Enabled decoders: aac/mp3/mp3float/pcm_s16le/h264; parsers: aac/h264/mpegaudio; demuxers: mov/mp3/wav; protocols: file; no encoders/hwaccels/muxers/filters/bsfs/indevs/outdevs; 'License: LGPL version 2.1 or later'; 'threading support: pthreads'; 'network support: no'). Two real bugs found and fixed getting there, neither FFmpeg-specific: (1) tools/crt-port-build.py's own build_configure_port() unconditionally indexed build['make_args'] with no .get() fallback -- every other configure-system recipe here (curl.json, freetype.json, ...) happens to always include make_args (even an empty list), a de facto required field this schema never documented as such; fixed by adding "make_args": [] here. (2) The clean configure run above was misleading -- config.mak's own CC=gcc line (found only by directly grepping it, since nothing failed loudly at configure time) revealed FFmpeg's own hand-rolled, non-autoconf configure script had silently fallen back to bare host gcc instead of this project's own tools/crt-cc, because it never read $CC from the environment (this project's own convention for every other, autoconf-based recipe here) -- it needs --cc= passed explicitly. Fixed by adding --cc=@ROOT@/tools/crt-cc, which then surfaced a second, genuinely useful bug: tools/crt-port-build.py's own configure_args substitution never applied @ROOT@ at all (only @CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@/@PORT_PREFIX@ were wired -- the exact same class of gap that function's own pre-existing comment already documents finding once before for @PORT_PREFIX@ during curl.json), so @ROOT@ passed through configure literally unsubstituted and failed configure's own compiler smoke test outright ('@ROOT@/tools/crt-cc is unable to create an executable file'). Fixed generally in tools/crt-port-build.py itself (not worked around locally here), matching the established precedent for the identical @PORT_PREFIX@ gap.

Windows target_overrides real bug found and fixed (2026-08-31, first Windows/MinGW build attempt): the original --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@ (this project's usual convention for every other, autoconf-based recipe's own windows override) is not a flag FFmpeg's own hand-rolled configure understands at all ('Unknown option "--build=x86_64-w64-mingw32"', confirmed directly by grepping configure's own option parser -- it has --arch=/--target-os=/--cross-prefix=/--toolchain=, no --build=/--host= autoconf-triple pair). Replaced with --arch=x86_64 --target-os=mingw32 --enable-cross-compile, the standard MinGW-w64 flag set (--cross-prefix not needed since --cc=@ROOT@/tools/crt-cc, already unconditional in the base configure_args, is a full, already-target-correct compiler wrapper on its own).

Windows: configure now succeeds cleanly (2026-08-31/09-01, after three real, non-FFmpeg-specific fixes -- see the --host-cc= and TMPDIR notes above/below -- confirmed via ./configure's own summary matching every intended decoder/demuxer/parser/protocol exactly, same as the Linux run), but the subsequent `make` step hits a real, currently-unresolved blocker: this project's own porting/recipes/make.json's Windows make.exe is deliberately built without HAVE_DOS_PATHS ('Windows intentionally uses the POSIX-like musl config path rather than the upstream Win32 make path so failures expose CRT/PAL gaps', that recipe's own notes) -- GNU Make's own internal path-absoluteness check (used when it needs to re-exec itself after one of the Makefiles it read gets remade as a side effect of a rule, which FFmpeg's real build graph genuinely triggers once, right after generating libavutil/libavcodec/libavformat/libswresample/libswscale's five *.version files) only recognizes a leading '/' as absolute without that define, so it treats a real, valid drive-letter path (e.g. C:/Users/.../make.exe) as relative and corrupts it by prepending its own current directory (observed literally: 'make.exe: <cwd>/C:/Users/.../make.exe: No such file or directory'). This is a genuine GNU Make self-re-exec bug exposed by FFmpeg's own build graph shape (no other Windows recipe ported here so far -- freetype/mbedtls/expat/xz/zlib/libffi, all flatter/non-restarting Makefile trees -- has ever exercised this particular GNU Make code path), not an FFmpeg configure_args problem, and NOT fixed in this pass: doing so safely needs its own dedicated investigation, since make.json's own HAVE_DOS_PATHS is a single, global (not per-recipe) build-time define for every already-'manual-pass'-verified Windows recipe's own make.exe, and HAVE_DOS_PATHS changes several of GNU Make's own internal semantics pervasively (path separator character, case sensitivity, backslash-as-separator handling) in ways that risk silently regressing those already-verified builds if done without equally careful, isolated re-verification of each one -- out of scope for this pass to attempt blind.

status.linux verified for real (2026-08-31): libcrtmedia's own crtmedia_demux_test (libcrtmedia/tests/demux_decode_test.c, gated behind CRTMEDIA_ENABLE_FFMPEG) demuxes+decodes a real project-authored WAV fixture (libcrtmedia/assets/test_tone.wav) end to end and reports the exact expected sample count (2000). Getting the *link* to succeed (source compiled cleanly with zero errors on the first real attempt, a genuinely positive surprise for a codebase this size) needed one more real, non-FFmpeg-specific fix beyond this file: libcrtmedia/CMakeLists.txt's own crtmedia STATIC target needed the same -Wl,--start-group/--end-group treatment libcrtgfx's own crtgfx target already established for the identical GNU-ld single-pass static-archive-scan-order problem (libavutil.a/libswresample.a's own sin/cos/memchr/... references landing, on a plain link, after libm.a/libc.a had already been scanned) -- with the *entire* PRIVATE static-lib set (c/m/dl/cxx) and the FFmpeg archives inside one contiguous group (splitting them across separate target_link_libraries() calls, even in the 'right' source order, was confirmed for real not to survive CMake's own link-line generation intact), and with the *consumer* (crtmedia_demux_test) not also linking c/m directly itself (doing so was confirmed for real to reposition them ahead of crtmedia's own grouped/forwarded copies, reintroducing the same bug from the consumer side). Full existing ctest suite re-run afterward: 106/107 passing, the one pre-existing failure (crtgfx_window_smoke_runs, needs a real display connection WSL headless doesn't have) unrelated to and unaffected by this change.

status.macos verified for real (2026-09-01, real macOS hardware): two real, macOS-specific bugs found and fixed, neither present on Linux. (1) `./configure`'s own `HAVE_SYSCTL` probe is a link-level `check_func`, not a real `#include <sys/sysctl.h>` compile check -- it passed (`libavutil/cpu.c` is then built with `#if HAVE_SYSCTL #include <sys/sysctl.h> ...`) because the real `sysctl()` *symbol* genuinely links fine against real Darwin libSystem, but `<sys/sysctl.h>` itself is not reachable through `tools/crt-cc`'s own `-nostdinc` + project sysroot include path at all (a real macOS/BSD-only header this project's Bionic-shaped sysroot was never going to carry) -- `fatal error: 'sys/sysctl.h' file not found`. This project's own libc already implements a portable equivalent (`sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`, confirmed real -- already used internally by libc/src/fd.c) that FFmpeg's own `avpriv_cpu_count()` falls back to automatically once `HAVE_SYSCTL` is 0 (the very next `#elif` branch in the same function) -- matching this project's established 'route a host-SDK-only path to the portable one already available, don't add a new Darwin-only shim for something POSIX already covers' policy (docs/porting_status.md's own sqlite-amalgamation entry states this explicitly). Fixed via `target_overrides.macos.post_configure_patch` (a pre-existing, generic tools/crt-port-build.py mechanism, not new): flips `#define HAVE_SYSCTL 1` to `0` in the generated `config.h` right after `./configure`, before `make` -- confirmed via grep this constant is used nowhere else in the whole tree this narrow `--disable-everything` build actually compiles, so the flip is fully scoped with no other side effect. (2) Once FFmpeg itself built and linked cleanly, `crtmedia_demux_test` (the real end-to-end test, not just a link check) crashed with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`/Bus error inside real Darwin `libsystem_pthread.dylib`'s own `pthread_once()`, called from `avcodec_find_decoder()`'s one-time codec-registration guard -- confirmed via `lldb`, not guessed: `x20` (the address `pthread_once` was dereferencing) pointed 4 bytes into FFmpeg's own `codec_mutex` global. Root-caused to a genuine ABI mismatch, not a logic bug: this executable's own real link line (`ninja -v`) put `-lSystem` *before* this project's own `libc.a` (which has its own real `pthread_once`, libc/src/pthread.c) -- Apple ld resolves an undefined symbol from the first thing that provides it regardless of archive-vs-dylib kind, so `-lSystem`'s real `pthread_once` satisfied the reference first and this project's own implementation, later in the link line inside `libc.a`, was never even consulted. `codec_mutex` itself was allocated using this project's own, much smaller `pthread_once_t` layout (the only `<pthread.h>` `crt-cc`'s own sysroot include path exposes to FFmpeg's source), but the function that actually ran against it was real Darwin's, which expects its own, differently-sized opaque `pthread_once_t` -- an out-of-bounds/misaligned access, not corruption. Fixed in `libcrtmedia/CMakeLists.txt`: `crtmedia_demux_test`'s own macOS branch now explicitly links `c m dl cxx` directly, before `System`, mirroring `crtmedia_frame_test`'s own pre-existing, already-working identical pattern just above it in the same file -- confirmed via `ninja -v` this moves `lib/libc.a` ahead of `-lSystem` on the real link line, and the test then passes for real end to end. Deliberately NOT applied to the Linux branch (which has its own, different, already-documented reason -- see this file's own 'Deliberately NOT linking c/m directly here' comment, libcrtmedia/CMakeLists.txt -- for omitting the exact same explicit link there): the two hosts need opposite treatment for the same-looking line, not a shared fix. Full ctest suite re-run afterward: 107/107 passing, no regressions.
